title: Dots and ties
summary: Two ways to make a note longer.

steps.title: Dotted note
steps.body:
A dot after a note makes it half as long again. A **dotted note** of a half note lasts 3 beats (2 + 1). A dotted quarter lasts 1½ beats.

**Why it matters:** The dotted quarter then eighth is one of the most common rhythms in pop, the "long-short" swing of countless choruses.

steps.title: Tie
steps.body:
A **tie** is a curved line joining two notes of the same pitch: play the first and hold it through the second, without playing again.

**Why it matters:** Ties let a note last across a bar line, which no single note can show.

steps.title: Two ways to last three beats
steps.body: A dotted half note, or a half note tied to a quarter: one tap, held for three beats.

items.prompt: Tap a dotted half note, then a quarter note: 2 taps.
Tap a dotted quarter, an eighth, then a half note: 3 taps.

steps.title: Long-short
steps.body: Play C as a dotted quarter, then an eighth, over and over. Sing "long, short, long, short".

items.prompt: How many quarter notes last as long as one dotted half note?
Tap a half note tied to a quarter note, then a quarter: 2 taps.
